name: Solo (German)
description: German Solo (often just 'Solo') is a trick-taking card game for 4 players that evolved from Quadrille and L'Hombre. It uses a 32-card deck (Aces down to 7s). It is distinct from Solo Whist. The unique feature is the 'Color' ranking (Clubs/Spades are black, Hearts/Diamonds are red) which affects the card order, and the presence of fixed top trumps called 'Matadors' (Spadille, Manille, Basto) regardless of the named trump suit.

overview.description: German Solo (often just 'Solo') is a trick-taking card game for 4 players that evolved from Quadrille and L'Hombre. It uses a 32-card deck (Aces down to 7s). It is distinct from Solo Whist. The unique feature is the 'Color' ranking (Clubs/Spades are black, Hearts/Diamonds are red) which affects the card order, and the presence of fixed top trumps called 'Matadors' (Spadille, Manille, Basto) regardless of the named trump suit.

history.origins: Dates back significantly to the 18th century as a simplified Quadrille. Retained the complex 'Ombre' ranking where black suits rank normally (K-Q-J-7-...) but red suits rank inversely in pip cards (A-2-3...).
timeline: 1800s: German Solo simplifies the 40-card game to 32 cards.
Present: Played by enthusiasts of historical games.
history.cultural: A game for intellectuals who enjoyed the complexity of variable card rankings.
history.evolution: The term 'Solo' refers to the bidder playing alone against three defenders.

setup.players: Four players. Each plays individually; temporary partnerships are formed by the outcome of bidding (in Frage or Grossfrage the declarer and the holder of the called ace are partners). Eldest hand sits to the dealer's left; deal rotates left after each hand.
setup.deck: A 32-card pack (Piquet or Skat pack): Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit. German- or French-suited; historically German-suited. Ranks 2 through 6 are removed from a standard 52-card deck.

rules.objective: Soloist wins 5 tricks (Simple) or all tricks (Tout).
rules.gameplay: After the deal, eldest hand bids first. Bids in ascending order are Frage, Grossfrage, and Solo; players may pass. In Frage, the declarer names a plain-suit ace they do not hold; whoever has it is the declarer's partner (secret until play). In Grossfrage, the declarer must hold both top matadors (Spadille and Manille) and again names an ace for a partner, who chooses trump (not the called ace's suit). In Solo, the declarer chooses trump and plays alone. Trick play: forehand leads; players must follow suit if possible; highest trump wins, or if no trump, highest card of the suit led. The declaring side must win at least five of the eight tricks. After taking the first five, they may stop for a prime bonus or continue; winning all eight is a Durchmarsch (slam).
keyRules: 32-card deck; 8 cards each. Deal in 3-2-3 or 4-2-2.
Bidding: Frage, Grossfrage, Solo in ascending order; eldest hand bids first.
Matadors (Spadille, Manille, Basto) are fixed top trumps; declarer names trump suit.
Follow suit if possible; trick winner leads next. Declarer side must take 5 tricks (or all 8 for Tout).

strategy.basic: Memorize the ranking. The complexity is the barrier. Spadille (Ace Spades) and Basto (Ace Clubs) are permanent trumps. If Hearts are trump, the Ace of Hearts (Pont) joins them. If Spades are trump, Spadille is just the Ace. Confusing? Yes. But critical.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Renouce': You must follow suit except when playing a Matador. Matadors can be held back even if you could follow suit (reneging privilege). Use this to save them for a game-winning trick.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Lead: Lead trumps to draw out the Soloist's Matadors. If they have none, you win easy.
tips: A black 7 is usually a low card unless it's the Manille.
Red Aces are low in plain suits but high in trump.

variations.name: Simple (5 tricks)
variations.description: Declarer or declarer's side must win at least 5 of 8 tricks to fulfill the contract.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes win condition to 5 tricks; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Tout (Durchmarsch)
variations.description: Declarer may announce Tout and attempt to win all 8 tricks for a bonus; may stop after 5 for prime bonus instead.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes win condition to all 8 tricks; no engine constant overrides needed.
